data.title: Retarget a licensed motion clip
data.summary: Source and target rigs, one 2-second walk and an explicit bone mapping. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Armatures provide bones, posing and skinning for character animation.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender animation / engine clips environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: Source and target rigs, one 2-second walk and an explicit bone mapping.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent retarget motion workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: Source and target rigs, one 2-second walk and an explicit bone mapping. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Compare rest poses, units and root conventions before mapping bones
Use the selected retargeting tool to create a separate target action
Correct contacts and bake a candidate; compare hips, feet and hands at keyframes

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned retarget a licensed motion clip candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: The target's feet reach the floor without changing body scale
Root displacement matches the chosen in-place/root-motion convention
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: Retargeting availability depends on the selected add-on or engine; Blender armatures alone do not imply automatic retargeting.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: A small mapping table is easier to audit than automatic guesses.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me retarget a licensed motion clip in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: Source and target rigs, one 2-second walk and an explicit bone mapping. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: The target's feet reach the floor without changing body scale; Root displacement matches the chosen in-place/root-motion convention. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.

troubleshooting.symptom: An operator, node socket or exporter option is unavailable
troubleshooting.action: Stop and inspect the installed tool/version documentation; adapt the smallest affected step rather than guessing an API name.

troubleshooting.symptom: The candidate fails its stated review condition
troubleshooting.action: Return to the last accepted source/parameter set, reduce to one representative case and record the failed observation. A small mapping table is easier to audit than automatic guesses.
